summary: Serinity Young was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. She earned her Ph.D. from Columbia University under Alex Wayman and studied with Vidya Dehejia, later working at the American Museum of Natural History and Southern Methodist University.
Sesso Oda was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under and succeeded traditional teacher Zuigan Goto. He taught students including Gary Snyder and Soko Morinaga.

Seung-yeon Lee works in Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. Lee completed doctoral studies under Sang-hae Lee and held posts at the Gyeonggi Institute of Cultural Properties and Sungkyunkwan University.

Seunghak Koh is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned an MA from Seoul National University and a PhD from UCLA under Robert E. Buswell Jr. Koh held a post as an Appointed Researcher at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies.

Seungsahn Haengwon was a Buddhist figure who studied at Dongguk University and under traditional teachers Ko Bong (succeeding him in 1957), Keumbong, and Geum-o. He founded the Kwan Um School of Zen in 1970 and taught numerous students.

Seán McLoughlin works in religious studies and Indology. He earned a Ph.D. from the University of Manchester and served as a Lecturer in South Asian, Islamic and Religious Studies at the University of Leeds.

Shagun Sinha works in computational fields, Indology, and linguistics. Sinha conducted doctoral studies under Girish Nath Jha and studied under teachers including Shashi Prabha Kumar, Ram Nath Jha, and C. Upender Rao.
Shailendra Bhandare is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He has held positions at the British Museum, Fitzwilliam Museum, Ashmolean Museum (as Assistant Keeper), and St Cross College.

Shaman Hatley is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied at Goddard College and completed a PhD at the University of Pennsylvania. He taught at Concordia University and became chair of Asian studies at the University of Massachusetts Boston.
Shan Shan Zhao is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who earned a Master of Arts at McMaster University under the supervision of James A. Benn, also studying with Shayne Clarke and Mark Rowe.

Shanshan Jia is a scholar of Indology and Tibetology pursuing doctoral studies at the University of Hamburg under Harunaga Isaacson, where she also held an appointment as a Wissenschaftliche Projektmitarbeiterin.

Shaoyong Ye is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who completed doctoral studies at Peking University under Qing Duan. He subsequently joined the faculty at Peking University, serving as an Associate Professor.
Sharon J. Roe is a scholar of religious studies and philosophy who earned a PhD at the California Institute of Integral Studies under the doctoral supervision of Steven D. Goodman.

Shashibhusan Dasgupta was an Indology, religious studies, and philosophy scholar. He studied at Brojomohun College, Scottish Church College, and the University of Calcutta (MA and PhD), where he served as a Lecturer from circa 1945 to 1964.

Shayne Clarke studied at Bukkyo University, the University of Canterbury (MA under Paul Harrison), and UCLA (PhD under Gregory Schopen). An Indology and Buddhist studies scholar, Clarke joined McMaster University and became a Research Fellow at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.
Shechen Rabjam Rinpoche is a figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under spiritual teacher Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche. He founded Karuna-Shechen in 2000.

Sheila Jasanoff studied at Radcliffe College, the University of Bonn, Harvard University, and Harvard Law School. She held faculty appointments at Cornell University from circa 1978 to 1998 and as a professor at Harvard Kennedy School from circa 1998.

Shek-Wing Tam was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied under Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje, Yingguang Qu, and Yui Chi Lau. He held posts at Renmin University of China and Tsinghua University, and founded the Sino-Tibetan Buddhist Studies Association.

Sheldon Pollock is an Indologist who completed his doctorate at Harvard University under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. He held professorships at the University of Iowa, the University of Chicago, and Columbia University, and founded the Murty Classical Library of India.

Sheng Yen was a Buddhist master and scholar who studied at Jing'an Temple Buddhist Academy and Rissho University. He founded the Chan Meditation Center, Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies, and Dharma Drum Mountain, holding posts at Shandao Temple and Chung-Hwa.
